features.note: Strong. compressor-room shows a solid walled box with a louvered access panel; compressor-room-open removes the walls and reveals the loose packages + receiver + dryer inside — walls clearly appear/disappear. exhaust-off shows the exterior louver panel with SHUT slats; exhaust-full shows the same panel with OPEN slats and two round exhaust fans visible behind them. Damper state change is unambiguous.

In luminaire-plan I can count discs in a roughly regular arrangement of ~6 rows x 3 columns (I count ~15-18 discernible caps; the outer rows fade into shadow so a few are inferred). In luminaire-grid and the compressor-room close-up the fixtures read clearly as UFO highbays: shallow finned aluminium disc with a bright lit lens underneath, hung on a stem. Regularity and fixture identity both hold.

bay-envelope shows a rooftop box (AHU) + smaller panel (condenser) on the closed roof. hero/duct-run show a continuous high-level trunk running the bay length with a vertical riser/drop off the AHU. Continuous air path reads. Weak point: the 'diffusers' along the trunk are green flow-direction cone gizmos rather than clearly modelled diffuser grilles, and the trunk reads as a shiny round tube more than a rectangular duct.

compressor-skid shows all four WITHOUT cropping: two rotary-screw packages (canopy box + round cooling-fan grille + ventilation louver panels on a base skid), a vertical domed receiver (navy cylinder), and a refrigerated dryer (louvered box), joined by real silver piping that rises to the high-level header. Identity is legible.

hero (roof off) shows clad perimeter walls, a column grid and a roof-truss framework with diagonal web/bracing at the ends. bay-envelope (roof on) reads as a genuinely CLOSED long-low building with rooftop units. Proportions read as a large industrial bay. Cladding is a bit flat/untextured but structurally convincing.

important_features.note: Piping rises from the receiver up to a high-level header that runs the length of the bay (visible in compressor-skid and hero); green flow cones mark direction along the header.

A ~1.8 m tan human figure stands on the slab in ahu-roof, duct-run and exhaust views. It reads as human-scaled but the mannequin is very crude (capsule head + block torso), so it only weakly conveys the 8 m height.

defects.detail: Along the trunk duct the 'diffusers' are green direction-arrow cones (interaction gizmos), not modelled supply diffusers; the trunk itself reads as a round polished tube rather than sheet-metal ductwork.
The scale human is a rough capsule/block mannequin; small and low-detail, limiting how strongly it sells the 8 m clear height.
In luminaire-plan the outer rows of the 6x3 array fall into shadow, so the full count of 18 is partly inferred rather than cleanly counted.

corrections.action: Add a few real rectangular supply diffusers on the underside of the trunk and hide the green flow-arrow gizmos in the beauty capture so 'trunk duct with diffusers' reads without relying on interaction markers.
Lift ambient/fill slightly for the plan capture so all 18 highbay caps are individually countable across the full 6x3 grid.
